transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-06-15
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Nina Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cruz (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Redwood Solutions), Alex Rivera (CTO, Nebula Ops), Priya Kaur (ML Eng), Mark Huang (Infra)

Summary: quick discovery focused on migration constraints from Anthropic/OpenAI, parity testing with vLLM/TGI, and clarifying hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs. Team requested pricing, pilot SOW, and a technical deep dive for on-prem considerations.

Topics: migration prerequisites; eval parity; latency vs cost; KV/prefix caching; private VPC/KMS; SOC2 & SSO compliance; pilot scope and timeline

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Nina: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Nina from Redwood, AE on this account, with Ethan and Samir. How are you all?
[00:05] Alex: Good, thanks. Busy but excited to talk through moving off our current provider.
[00:09] Priya: Hey. We kinda want to, uh, validate parity and make sure we don't regress on hallucinations or latency.
[00:13] Ethan: Totally. That's our bread and butter — helping teams map eval parity and figure out the hosting option that fits. Quick ask before we dive: are you primarily on Anthropic or OpenAI today?
[00:20] Alex: A mix. We use OpenAI for prod for most chat flows but have some workloads on Anthropic and a few internal experiments on vLLM locally. We also run a small TGI stack for reranking.
[00:29] Mark: And infra wise we run GCP for most services, some Azure for legacy. We're evaluating whether to stay hosted or reserve dedicated capacity, or do a private on-prem for regulated clients.
[00:38] Nina: Great. Can you walk us through the success criteria — what parity means for you? Latency, cost per token, output quality?
[00:45] Priya: All three. Primary is quality — we have a set of 3k prompts and scoring harness. Second is p99 latency under 400ms for short queries. Third is total cost, obviously.
[00:55] Samir: Do you have a sample of those prompts and the scoring harness?
[00:58] Priya: We can share a bucket link, yeah. We'll sanitize a few examples.
[01:01] Ethan: Perfect. Our typical approach: baseline your OpenAI/Anthropic runs, then match on Redwood hosted first and run a parity pass. If needed we spin up Dedicated to hit throughput or Private for compliance. We also have suggestions for quant profiles and batching to reduce cost.
[01:18] Alex: Two big blockers: 1) KMS/HSM integration for FIPS stuff, and 2) on-prem network isolation for certain clients. Are those supported?
[01:27] Nina: Yes — Private supports customer-managed KMS and can be deployed in VPCs. For on-prem we have an air-gapped package, but that's a longer lead time.
[01:36] Mark: When you say customer-managed KMS, do you mean we can bring keys into HSM and Redwood won't see plaintext? We need to confirm the encryption chain.
[01:43] Samir: Short answer yes, you can manage keys and we integrate with KMS/HSM, and logs are configurable for the control plane vs data plane. We'll follow up with the security docs.
[01:50] Priya: Do you have SOC 2 and ISO attestations? Our security team will ask.
[01:54] Nina: SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 reports are available. We'll attach compliance pack.
[01:58] Alex: Cool. On the technical side, our vLLM runs locally with a lot of prefix caching and custom kv cache handling. Subtle differences in KV semantics have caused regressions before. How do you handle KV cache and prefix caching?
[02:10] Ethan: That's a great question. Our runtime supports KV cache sharding and prefix caching — automatic prefix detection for repeated prompts. There are differences in how vLLM/TGI implement cache tokens, so we include a compatibility layer and canonicalization step in the migration guide.
[02:23] Priya: When you say canonicalization, do you rewrite tokenization or handle EOS differences? We saw tokenization drift when switching from OpenAI to local vLLM.
[02:31] Ethan: Some tokenization drift is expected. Our parity tests include tokenization normalization and we provide tokenizer mapping tools. For EOS and stop-token semantics we have adapters for TGI-based stacks.
[02:39] Alex: Can you run our 3k prompt harness and show a head-to-head with current provider? We're looking for a quantitative report.
[02:45] Nina: Yes — that's part of the pilot. Typically we run a baseline on your snapshot, run hosted Redwood with same model versions, and report quality/regression metrics + latency/cost.
[02:53] Mark: About model versions: we pin versions in production. If you auto-route to quantized variants for cost savings, how do we ensure deterministic behavior?
[03:02] Samir: We let customers pin model variants; automatic fallback to quantized or lower-tier happens only under configured policies. For determinism we support model version pinning and can freeze the execution profile during the pilot.
[03:12] Priya: Any known differences for RLHF-style prompts? We saw some scoring differences moving between Anthropic and OpenAI.
[03:19] Ethan: RLHF differences often come from subtle model implementation and decoding defaults. We recommend matching sampling parameters (temperature, top_p) and doing eval-based calibration. We'll include an RLHF parity checklist.
[03:29] Alex: Latency — you mentioned p99 targets. Our busiest endpoint sees bursts up to 700 qps. What options do we have?
[03:36] Ethan: For that scale we'd recommend Dedicated pools with autoscaling and burst capacity. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and capacity isolation. For cost control we can suggest batching and a hybrid routing policy (hosted for low-volume or experimental endpoints, dedicated for heavy production).
[03:49] Mark: How do you handle cold starts and kv cache warmup for bursts?
[03:52] Samir: We do proactive cache warming based on traffic patterns and support continuous batching. For stateful KV warmups we can pre-warm minibatches. We'll need sample traffic profile to size it.
[04:02] Priya: On model compatibility — we run some proprietary fine-tuned checkpoints on top of base models with TGI. Can Redwood host customer-built checkpoints?
[04:10] Nina: Yes; Redwood supports customer model uploads and private model hosting in Dedicated or Private. We have model signing and storage controls.
[04:16] Alex: Any known gotchas moving from OpenAI embeddings to Redwood embeddings? We use embeddings heavily for search.
[04:22] Ethan: Embedding vectors vary by model. We often recommend reindexing when switching model family. For near-zero drift, you can run a split test and compare recall at top-k. We'll help craft an embedding migration plan.
[04:33] Mark: Pricing question — what's the delta between hosted and dedicated per token? Ballpark.
[04:38] Nina: Ballpark hosted is easier to start with and has usage pricing. Dedicated is commit-based and typically lower per-token at scale but requires a monthly commitment. We'll send ranges in the follow-up pricing doc — depends on model class and qps.
[04:48] Priya: We need to keep costs under a threshold for this year. Also want to avoid re-architecting our stack too much.
[04:54] Ethan: Understood. That's why the pilot focuses on a single critical flow so we can prove cost parity or improvements before a bigger migration.
[05:00] Alex: Security/attestation detail — audit logs and sensitive data redaction. Our compliance team requires immutable audit trails and ability to redact PII.
[05:09] Samir: We provide audit logs with configurable retention and redaction hooks in the private deployments. Hosted has role-based access and log export; for the highest requirements, Private gives you full control.
[05:19] Mark: For Private, what's the lead time?
[05:21] Nina: On-prem/air-gapped is the longest — usually a few months depending on scope. Private in customer VPC is faster, often weeks, depending on network approvals.
[05:31] Priya: For the parity run, can you replicate our local vLLM custom layers? We depend on a patched vllm backend.
[05:37] Ethan: We can run parity using your vLLM stack as a reference, but for production we typically standardize on the Redwood runtime. If your custom patches are required we can discuss a Private deployment that runs your binaries or a shim.
[05:49] Alex: How do you handle support SLAs during pilot?
[05:52] Nina: Pilot includes standard support; Dedicated/Enterprise bundles include higher SLAs and an assigned CSM. We'll capture required SLA in the SOW.
[05:59] Priya: Regression monitoring — do you have hooks for prompt-set based alerting?
[06:03] Samir: Yes, Redwood Optimize integrates evals and will alert on regression thresholds tied to your prompt sets. We can wire that into your existing dashboards.
[06:11] Alex: Any references — other customers who did similar migration from Anthropic/OpenAI with vLLM parity?
[06:16] Nina: We have a couple of anonymized case studies — we'll share one where we ran a 4-week parity and reduced cost 22% while maintaining output quality.
[06:25] Mark: Networking — do you support private peering or direct connect to GCP/Azure?
[06:29] Ethan: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we support private peering and direct connect configurations.
[06:33] Priya: One more: how deterministic are outputs with quantized kernels? We've seen variability with int8 quant and certain top-k configs.
[06:41] Ethan: Quantization can introduce slight distributional changes. Our Optimize team has validated quant profiles per model to minimize drift. For sensitive flows you can run with FP16 or pinned kernels during the pilot.
[06:52] Alex: Timeline — we want a 6-week pilot to validate parity on one major endpoint. Is that feasible?
[06:57] Nina: Yes, 4–8 weeks is common. We'll propose a 6-week pilot in the SOW.
[07:02] [Speaker 1]: (inaudible)
[07:05] Priya: Cool. Logistics: we'll share the prompt harness, sample traffic, and a list of high-sensitivity flows.
[07:11] Mark: And access to our current metrics dashboards so you can compare latency and request traces.
[07:14] Samir: Great. We'll need a short authorization to pull baseline metrics — or you can share a slice.
[07:18] Alex: We'll share. Also procurement question — any standard contract addendum for data residency?
[07:22] Nina: We have template addenda for data residency and encryption clauses. We'll include in the follow-up.
[07:27] Priya: If we proceed, expected next week for the technical deep dive?
[07:31] Nina: We can schedule a technical deep dive with our infra SEs next Tuesday.
[07:35] Alex: Works.
[07:36] Ethan: I'll prepare the parity checklist and a benchmark script that runs your harness with our hosted endpoints.
[07:41] Mark: One last concern — fallback behavior. If Redwood is serving and we see a regression, do you automatically failover to our previous provider?
[07:48] Samir: We support routing policies that can fallback to an external provider, but that requires planning in the routing config. It's doable, we just need to define compatibility mapping.
[07:57] Alex: Good to know.
[07:58] Nina: Ok recap: Nina sends pricing + pilot SOW; Ethan sends parity checklist + benchmark script; Mark shares traffic profile; Priya shares prompt harness; schedule technical deep dive next Tuesday. Anything missing?
[08:12] Priya: Please include security docs and KMS/HSM integration details.
[08:16] Nina: We'll attach SOC2/ISO and KMS integration notes.
[08:19] Alex: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the follow-up.
[08:22] Nina: Thanks all. We'll follow up by end of week.

Notes on transcription: occasional word swap (vLLM/vell em), mis-heard acronyms (TGI as T G I), and speaker overlap. Links mentioned: security pack (link to be shared), parity checklist (to be attached), pilot SOW (to be shared).

End of transcript.
